audit_findings.title: The anchor may precede another margin step-down
audit_findings.magnitude: First-half 2026 operating income fell $231.840 million, or 24.1%; excluding the $134.5 million tariff refund, the decline was $366.340 million, or 38.1%. A sustained anchor-OE reduction of approximately $500.6 million, or 32.0%, would reduce the base 30%-MOS buy-below from $143.91 to the $100.61 market price.
audit_findings.mechanism: A further earnings decline before scenario growth begins would reduce the OE anchor and every forecast-period cash flow and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on the current landscape, mitigating actions are not expected to fully offset the effect of imposed tariffs and the removal of the de minimis exemption, and we expect continued decline in our gross margin and operating margin in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: Current deterioration is demonstrated: first-half operating margin fell from 19.7% to 14.9% despite a material tariff refund. Whether margins and OE decline further is unresolved, but the underlying operating-income decline is large enough relative to the approximately 32% anchor reduction needed to erase the base-case purchase margin. The flat bear path therefore does not adequately bound the presently evidenced risk.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the first forecast year from quarterly 2026 results, exclude nonrecurring tariff refunds, explicitly model tariffs, lost de minimis treatment and mitigation, and rerun all scenarios with any resulting FY2026 OE decline occurring before growth begins.

audit_findings.title: A committed lease is absent from both the recorded liability and anchor expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $278.5 million of undiscounted minimum lease commitments, equal to 13.2% of the $2,103.820 million recorded minimum operating-lease payments; annual expense and associated facility economics are unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: After commencement, distribution-center rent and related operating costs reduce OE, while any capacity, service or efficiency benefits may increase revenue or margins; it is not a separate debt deduction from the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 1, 2026, the Company's minimum lease commitment for distribution center operating leases which have been committed to, but not yet commenced, was $ 278.5 million, which is not reflected in the table above.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted commitment is demonstrated, but its annual expense, commencement profile and incremental economics are not supplied. The total commitment cannot be treated as a one-year OE charge, and the record cannot determine whether the facility is value-dilutive or supports sufficient growth and efficiency to offset its costs.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the lease commencement date, term and annual base-rent schedule plus expected staffing, depreciation and logistics savings; incorporate the net annual economics into each scenario without deducting the lease obligation again in the equity bridge.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may not be fully distributable to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $89.1 million; 6.4% of the $1,389.737 million cash bridge, 0.38% of $23,377 million base equity value and $0.78 per diluted share. A full deduction would lower the 30%-MOS buy-below by approximately $0.55 to $143.36.
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental repatriation tax would reduce the cash and short-term-investment amount added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The unrecognized deferred income tax liability on the indefinitely reinvested amount is approximately $ 89.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The unrecognized tax estimate is filed, although the record does not establish that repatriation is required or that all of it relates to the latest cash balance. Even conservatively deducting the entire $89.1 million leaves the adjusted buy-below about $42.75 above the $100.61 market price, so this item cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile latest cash by jurisdiction and available paid-up capital, then rerun the bridge net of any incremental withholding and state taxes; retain the existing conclusion unless the reconciliation identifies taxes materially beyond the filed $89.1 million estimate.

audit_findings.title: Inventory growth raises a markdown and working-capital normalization risk
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest net inventory was $1,711.450 million, down 1% year over year; provisions and reserves were $99.526 million, up $10.703 million from February 1, 2026. Any reserve deficiency or future markdown loss is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional markdowns or inventory provisions increase cost of goods sold and reduce OE; structurally higher inventory requirements consume working capital and reduce distributable cash.
audit_findings.evidence: Our inventory balance as of February 1, 2026 was $1.7 billion, an increase of 18% from February 2, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The earlier 18% annual inventory increase was real, but the latest filing shows inventory down year over year and only a $14.350 million first-half cash outflow for inventory versus $237.903 million in the prior-year period. No reserve deficiency is demonstrated. Weak comparable sales and lower conversion still create a forward-looking markdown risk, so the issue warrants monitoring rather than a current valuation correction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain inventory units, aging, full-price sell-through, outlet exposure and reserve coverage by market and category; rerun normalized OE if subsequent markdowns, write-downs or sustained inventory funding exceed the amounts already reflected in results.

audit_findings.title: A favorable PSU expense reversal remains in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.3 million pre-tax, or 1.68% of the $1,564.9 million anchor OE. A conservative dollar-for-dollar removal would reduce base operating value by approximately $369.5 million, base value by $3.25 per share and the 30%-MOS buy-below by approximately $2.27 to $141.64.
audit_findings.mechanism: If included, the nonrecurring compensation credit raises the OE anchor and proportionately raises forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Therefore, we recognized a reversal of stock-based compensation expense of $26.3 million during the second quarter of 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $26.3 million reversal is demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether the 2026 latest-actual anchor still includes the second-quarter 2025 credit. Even assuming full inclusion and conservatively removing the pre-tax amount dollar for dollar from OE, the adjusted buy-below remains approximately $41.03 above the $100.61 market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map the $1,564.9 million anchor's measurement window to the affected quarter; if the reversal is included, remove it or substitute normalized PSU expense and rerun the valuation.
